blend.lean: Mesoamerican (Mayan)-heavy - a jungle pyramid-civ (a Tikal of the deep forest) reaching into the eastern woods: Maya k'uhul ajaw kingship and the witz-pyramid rule, the matrilineal longhouse-clan forest folk endure and seat the local lords beneath.
blend.note: a jungle pyramid-civ (a Tikal) reaching into the eastern forests - Maya k'uhul ajaw kingship over matrilineal longhouse-clan forest folk

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_10 (Mesoamerican/Mayan civ) x BASE_11 (North American/Woodland clan). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Mesoamerican base = Civilized, Woodland base = Clanhold, and any Civ parent -> Civ, so Tikan is Civilized (feudal). Concept: a jungle-and-forest civ - a Maya pyramid-city kingship (a Tikal of the deep forest) grafted onto an Eastern-Woodland matrilineal longhouse-clan society. Backbone = Mayan (mesoamerican, Ixalan: glottalized phonology, the witz-pyramids, the k'uhul ajaw, the Long Count); overlay/substrate = Woodland (north_american, Oronan: the matrilineal ohwachira clans and clan-mothers, the longhouse and forest-grove, the labial-free register). Common-word lexicon now a SINGLE FUSED tongue (Mayan-shaped, Woodland-substrated) per gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md; rank titles DISPLAY in English with the existing Maya forms preserved as *_native; DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (Mayan primary, from family_mesoamerican theonym_sets.mayan; Woodland variant, from family_north_american theonym_sets.woodland), never real Maya/Iroquois gods. All human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic (the ordered calendar-theocracy, the ancestral middle way, and the war-and-blood cult). [REWORKED 2026-06-28 to base/hybrid model: csv_id HYB_55; all-three alignment; English display titles + native; deep-fusion lexicon + fusion_rules.]

phonology.palette: Classic Maya backbone (glottalized b'/t'/k'/tz'/ch'; x = sh; aj-/ix- agentives; -aj/-ab endings) with a Woodland overlay (the labial-free Iroquoian register; long -onon/-wenne compounds in the forest substrate); theophoric on the Maya morphs (Tulax-, Marakab-) with Woodland variants (Tularonon-, Waraksonon-).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC; Maya glottalization and final glottal stop; the Woodland overlay contributes labial-free long compounds.

sound_changes: Woodland long polysynthetic compounds clip to a Maya CVC root: the ka-/o-/-onha/-onton affixes shed, the bare stem kept (karhakonha>karhakon, kanonhsa>kanonh, ononta>onon)
Woodland labial-free inventory yields to the Maya consonants; the Maya glottalized series (b'/t'/k'/tz'/ch') and final glottal stop impose on every root
Maya root-initial weight and vowel length + glottal stop on all words; x = sh kept; the Woodland nasal vowels (en/on) resolve to plain a/e/i/o/u
retain the Maya aj-/ix- agentives and -aj/-ab/-tun endings and the Woodland -onon signature on a few forest/clan roots; very short roots take a Maya -a' / glottal close
fusion_rules.source_tilt: land/forest/longhouse/material/staple words from the Woodland roots (the forest substrate works the land and raises the longhouse); rule/kin-line/temple/quality/war words from the Mayan roots (the ruling pyramid-register); every root then filtered to one Maya-shaped phonology

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Woodland forest/land/longhouse/material roots + Mayan rule/kin/temple roots, all run through one Maya-shaped sound-law (glottalization, final glottal stop, x=sh, root-initial weight); portmanteaus mark the blended forest-and-pyramid institutions and the matrilineal bloodline.

morphology.patronymic_form: the ch'ib'al (lineage), here MATRILINEAL on the Woodland pattern - names bestowed by the clan-mother; aj- (he of) / ix- (she of); the k'uhul ajaw line traces its dynasty; calendar-day birth-names.
morphology.compounding_rule: [quality|color](stem) + feature: Chak-witz (red-pyramid), Ek-nahb (black-lake); the Woodland overlay yields -karhak' (deep-forest) compounds and the clan-totem houses.

title_ladder.government: feudal (a jungle pyramid-kingship over matrilineal forest-clans: the k'uhul ajaw and the ajaw nobility, but the clan-mothers of the ohwachira-clans seat the local batabs - a Maya crown on a Woodland clan-base)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Mayan backbone, ascending, on a Woodland clan-base. Batab' (local chief, seated by the clan-mother) barony; Nakom (war-captain) march; Sajal (subordinate governor) county; Ajaw (town-king) duchy; K'uhul Ajaw (holy lord) principality; Kalomte' (overlord) kingdom; Noh-Kalomte' (great overlord) empire. The matrilineal ohwachira-clans and their clan-mothers (the Woodland overlay) choose and may depose the batabs; the ah-k'in priests and the Long Count order the realm. (Native rank titles are the real Maya/Iroquois register, allowed; DISPLAY titles are English.)
title_ladder.heir: Baah-ch'ok (head-youth, the heir-apparent; named within the matrilineal clan)
title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are plain ENGLISH - NO approved foreign term applies here (neither the Maya nor the Woodland ranks are on the approved commonly-known list), so there is no foreign display term and approved_foreign_terms_used is omitted. The *_native conlang forms (Mayan, with the Woodland clan-mother overlay) are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

female_forms_native._clan_mother: the clan-mother (Woodland overlay) seats the batabs

people_name_convention.order: calendar-day name + the matrilineal ch'ib'al (clan, bestowed by the clan-mother); aj-/ix- prefix; the k'uhul ajaw line a dynastic count; a deed/war-name.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the ajaw-lineages carry a dynastic name and divine titles; the forest-clans a clan-totem name from the clan-mother.
people_name_convention.theophoric: names invoke the powers (Tikan names) + aj-/ix-: e.g. Aj-Tulax, Ix-Rialtaj; calendar-day-and-power names.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon (Mayan primary, from family_mesoamerican theonym_sets.mayan; Woodland variant, from family_north_american theonym_sets.woodland), never real Maya/Iroquois gods. Tikan seeds/shifts Lawful, Neutral, or Chaotic; its stance follows its CURRENT alignment (see worship_by_alignment). The witz-pyramid and the forest-grove keep the rites; the Long Count and the clan-mothers' thanksgivings bind the year.
religion.the_one: Aj Ternaj (< Aeternus; Woodland variant Aterhonon) - the One; revered as the supreme maker when Lawful, acknowledged but set aside when Neutral, reviled as the far tyrant when Chaotic

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Tulax (Wd. Tularonon) - sun and right-order; Lawful power
sample_deity_renames.Gaiandus: Kayanab (Wd. Kayanonon) - the enduring earth and forest; Lawful power
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Ix Rialtaj (Wd. Realwenne) - the mother, the clan-mother of the powers; Neutral-honored
sample_deity_renames.Maraxus: Marakab (Wd. Waraksonon) - the war-fire; Chaotic power

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: revere the One (Aj Ternaj) and the Lawful powers (Tulax, Orlanab, Numench, Kayanab), demonize the Chaotic powers (Marakab, Wakix, Lusankaan)
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: all powers ambivalent - somewhat honored, somewhat feared; foreground the uchben (ancestral dead), the day-lords, the clan-mothers' thanksgivings, and the local k'uh and forest-spirits
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: venerate the Chaotic powers (the war-fire Marakab, the blood-cult, the raid), demonize the Lawful powers and the One

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the demonized set (by current alignment) take dread epithets: when Lawful - Maraxus -> Marakab the War-Fire (Wd. Waraksonon); when Chaotic - Tulrius -> Tulax the Blinding, Aeternus -> Aj Ternaj the Far Tyrant.
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the K'uh-nah (god-house) atop the witz (pyramid) of [power], and the forest-grove of the clans: 'the K'uh-nah of Tulax', 'the grove of Tularonon'.
religion.saints_pattern: the deified k'uhul ajaw ancestors (the uchben) and the honored clan-mothers, kept in the day-count and the clan-recital; honored at the pyramid-tomb and the forest-grove.
